clinicalPearls: Caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC25A1, the mitochondrial citrate carrier (citrate-malate antiporter) — biochemically distinct from the two single 2-hydroxyglutaric acidurias because both the D- and L-enantiomers accumulate together.
Presents as a severe neonatal-onset epileptic encephalopathy with profound hypotonia, intractable seizures, respiratory insufficiency and essentially absent psychomotor development.
Structural brain malformations are common, particularly agenesis or hypoplasia of the corpus callosum and simplified gyration.
Urine organic acids show elevation of both D-2- and L-2-hydroxyglutarate; chiral (enantiomer-resolving) separation confirms the combined pattern.
An allelic congenital myasthenic syndrome (SLC25A1-related, CMS23) sits at the milder end of the SLC25A1 spectrum and should be recognised in relatives.
The citrate carrier exports mitochondrial citrate to the cytosol for fatty acid and sterol synthesis; its loss disrupts carbon shuttling and the 2-hydroxyglutarate/2-oxoglutarate balance.
Prognosis is poor with frequent early death, and management is supportive.
reference.pathophysiology: Combined D,L-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC25A1, which encodes the mitochondrial citrate carrier (tricarboxylate carrier), an inner-membrane transporter that exchanges cytosolic malate for mitochondrial citrate and isocitrate. Loss of transport impairs export of citrate required for cytosolic lipogenesis and sterol synthesis and perturbs the interconnected 2-hydroxyglutarate/2-oxoglutarate pool, so both D-2- and L-2-hydroxyglutarate accumulate simultaneously — the biochemical signature that separates this condition from the single-enantiomer acidurias caused by defective enantiomer-specific dehydrogenases. The resulting disturbance of neuronal energy and biosynthetic metabolism produces a severe neonatal epileptic encephalopathy, often accompanied by structural brain malformation.
additionalDifferentials: L-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria (L2HGDH) — childhood leukoencephalopathy, cerebellar ataxia and increased brain tumour risk
Other neonatal epileptic encephalopathies (KCNQ2, STXBP1, pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy)
Nonketotic hyperglycinaemia and other neonatal metabolic encephalopathies
Mitochondrial energy-failure encephalopathies with structural brain anomalies
Congenital myasthenic syndromes (for the milder allelic SLC25A1 phenotype)
additionalInvestigations: Urine organic acids with chiral separation of D- and L-2-hydroxyglutarate
Plasma and CSF 2-hydroxyglutarate and amino acid profiles
SLC25A1 gene sequencing or metabolic gene panel
Brain MRI assessing the corpus callosum, gyral pattern and white matter
EEG to characterise the seizure and encephalopathy pattern
Blood lactate and general metabolic screen
Echocardiography and systemic examination for associated anomalies
redFlags: Neonatal intractable seizures with profound hypotonia and no developmental progress
Respiratory failure requiring support in the newborn period
Structural brain malformation on imaging in the setting of an organic aciduria
Rapid clinical deterioration in the neonatal period
reference.prognosis: The combined form is severe: most affected neonates have profound neurological impairment and many die in infancy or early childhood, with care remaining supportive.
pitfalls: Measuring total 2-hydroxyglutarate without chiral separation, which can miss the combined both-enantiomer signature.
Attributing the picture to a single 2-HGA subtype and halting the diagnostic workup.
Overlooking the milder allelic congenital myasthenic phenotype in a relative.
Assuming that a structural brain malformation excludes an underlying metabolic cause.
management: Aggressive antiseizure therapy, often combining agents, for the intractable neonatal-onset epileptic encephalopathy
Respiratory support, including ventilatory assistance, for the associated respiratory insufficiency
Nutritional support by nasogastric or gastrostomy feeding for the profound hypotonia and feeding difficulty
Supportive neurodevelopmental and comfort care with early palliative-care involvement given the severe prognosis and high early mortality
Coordinate care through neonatology, metabolic medicine, neurology and palliative-care teams
Offer genetic counselling and SLC25A1 family testing, including recognition of the allelic congenital myasthenic syndrome in relatives
